fields.name: Barnard's Star
fields.description: Official test target. Highest proper-motion star in the sky (~10.4"/yr): ~1.9 SPHEREx pixels over the DR1+QR3 baseline (1.66 px measured offline on the FITS files between the Aug 2025 and Aug 2026 seasons). Saturated core: image brightness is not a measurement.

fields.name: Epsilon Indi B
fields.description: Official test target. Pair of T brown dwarfs (Ba+Bb, unresolved at 6.15"/px) orbiting the bright star eps Ind A, ~402" away. ~1.1 SPHEREx pixels of motion over the baseline.

fields.name: R Draconis
fields.description: Official test target. Mira variable (catalog period 245.6–247.2 d), 8.6° from the north ecliptic pole. Saturated in every exposure: measured offline in the PSF wings on all 2,493 SPHEREx exposures, it shows a 0.5–1.3 mag cycle of ~260 d in 2025–2026, in phase with AAVSO. The light curve below uses the wide survey only (539 exposures), so its period range (240–276 d) cannot tell ~260 d from the catalog value. Image brightness here is not a measurement.

fields.name: RW Aurigae
fields.description: Official test target. Young T Tauri star (A+B, 1.5" apart, unresolved): it does not move, it changes brightness. Saturated in D2–D6; measured offline on unsaturated D1 exposures at matched wavelength, it brightened by about 1 mag (0.75–0.77 µm) from Sep 2025 to Sep 2026. In the B/W blink only the D1 frames can show it (a 2.6x display-level brightness ratio between 2025W36_1A_0233_3D1 and 2026W37_1A_0234_3D1, measured on the published images); the D2–D6 cores are saturated. Brightness for science comes from the FITS light curve below, which plots those D1 measurements of the blended pair; saturation removes most exposures of the bright state.

fields.name: WISE 0855−0714
fields.description: Official test target. Coldest known brown dwarf, ~2.3 pc away, ~8.2"/yr. Extremely red (J=25, W2=13.7): SPHEREx sees it only at 3.8–5.0 µm (D5–D6), faint in single exposures. Only DR1 data so far: ~1.4 SPHEREx pixels of motion.

systems.name: Barnard's Star system
systems.description: Challenge test target: the fastest-moving star in our sky, with four small planets.

systems.name: Epsilon Indi system
systems.description: Challenge test target: an orange dwarf star, a cold giant planet and a pair of brown dwarfs.

systems.name: R Draconis
systems.description: Challenge test target: a giant star that swells and fades every ~8 months.

systems.name: RW Aurigae
systems.description: Challenge test target: a young binary star whose dusty disk causes deep dimming events.

systems.name: WISE 0855−0714
systems.description: Challenge test target: the coldest known brown dwarf, near the freezing point of water.
